title: AXI Deadlock Hunt: Channel Dependency Analysis
description: Trace a channel-dependency deadlock from a signal log, classify each wait as a protocol violation or a legal policy, write protocol checks plus labelled service watchdogs, then prove the fixed master completes.

steps.title: Step 1: Run and Observe
steps.instructions: Compile testbench.sv with axi_deadlock_checker.sv in a local SystemVerilog simulator and run it with no plusarg. The write and the read never complete; the run stops at the 2000 ns TIMEOUT watchdog. Record which VALID and READY signals are HIGH and LOW in the signal log while it is stuck.

steps.title: Step 2: Analyze the Dependency
steps.instructions: Read the master stimulus and the strict_slave in testbench.sv. Draw the wait-for graph: what the master's WVALID waits for, what the slave's AWREADY waits for, and why the read hangs too. Classify each wait as a protocol violation or a legal policy, and explain why the slave's AWREADY is driven from a register.

steps.title: Step 3: Complete Protocol Checks and Service Watchdogs
steps.instructions: Edit axi_deadlock_checker.sv. Add separate AW, W, AR, B, and R VALID/payload stability properties, count AW, WLAST and B handshakes to check that BVALID follows both the AW and the WLAST handshake, then add the gated AW/W/AR service-bound checks, labelled as an integration contract and reporting once per stall.

steps.title: Step 4: Fix the Master and Prove Progress
steps.instructions: Read the +FIX_MASTER branch of the master stimulus, predict the edge of every handshake, then rerun with +FIX_MASTER. The write and the read must both complete against the same strict slave, with zero failures from your checker while the service bounds stay enabled.
